text: GUARDRAILS / RETIREMENT / APPROACH [prop labels: RETIREMENT FUND on the sack]
scene: A cartoon older man with swept-back grey hair, round glasses and a grey beard wears a burgundy velvet robe with gold trim and holds up one open palm. In the other hand he carries a burlap sack labelled RETIREMENT FUND with gold coins at its mouth. At the far left, a gold-posted rope barrier stands in front of stacked banknote bundles, gold bars and coins, and a curved green arrow below the last word sweeps back toward the sack.
mechanism: A gate-keeping metaphor: the raised palm and the brass stanchions guarding the cash literally picture 'guardrails', while the headline column names the topic.
composition: The man stands left of centre at near full height, with the money barrier at the left edge and a three-line headline stack filling the right 55 percent of the frame. The figure and the text column are balanced about equally, so the eye has two competing anchors; the green arrow bends back to link them.
typography: Three black block words stack top to bottom, with RETIREMENT reversed to white on a red bar; all three are readable at 160x90 and the middle word is the loudest. The words reuse the title's own terms in a new order and add no fact the title lacks.
colors: Pure white ground with black text, one red label bar and a green arrow as the only saturated accents. The burgundy robe and gold trim give the figure a warm, separate silhouette against the white.
psychology: Half-lidded eyes with slightly lowered brows, one raised open palm, and an upright stance read as a stop-and-listen teacher pose. Nothing in the image signals fear or urgency.
partnership: The thumbnail echoes the title's three key nouns and illustrates the barrier idea, so it mostly duplicates rather than adds. The open question of what the guardrails actually are is left for the video.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: red RETIREMENT bar first, then the man's face and raised hand, then the money behind the rope at left, and finally the green arrow and APPROACH.
art: Smooth glossy cartoon with a consistent outline and soft shading on the robe, clean cutout against white. The sack, rope posts and banknotes are all coherent and the white background keeps the frame uncluttered at small size.
strength: The rope-barrier-around-cash image is a literal, instantly readable picture of the word guardrails.
weakness: Headline words are reordered title copy, so the text adds nothing new, and the retirement-bag prop is small.
bottleneck: Nothing makes the viewer curious about the specific rule or number, so the frame reads as a generic retirement-advice explainer.
action: Hypothesis: replace APPROACH with a concrete guardrail figure (for example a percentage band written on the barrier) to test whether specificity beats the abstract label.
mechanism_secondary: metaphor of a barrier around money
counterexample: Seq 22 uses a point-and-shout headline with a concrete ETF chart, giving specific numbers where this frame stays abstract.
expression_label: half-lidded gaze with raised open palm
hero_object: retirement fund sack and rope-barrier money stack
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: It Dies / EVERY NIGHT
scene: A large hummingbird with a green crown, bulging round eyeballs and a wide-open beak takes up the left half of the frame. Its body is translucent ice-blue with icicles hanging from both wings and the beak tip, and small water droplets float beside the head. A thin black hand-drawn arrow curves from under the text toward the bird.
mechanism: A stark consequence statement paired with a frozen, screaming animal makes the title's complaint concrete: the bird's nightly death is shown as ice.
composition: The bird occupies about 45 percent of the frame at the left with its beak pointing across to the text on the right; the arrow closes the loop back to the bird. White negative space below the text keeps the layout open and the bird the clear primary focus.
typography: Four words over two lines: a thin hand-lettered mixed-case It Dies (capital I and D) above heavy capitals EVERY NIGHT, black on white. EVERY NIGHT survives well at 160x90 while the lighter It Dies line is thinner, and the text adds a claim the title does not state.
colors: Cold teal and cyan on the bird against a clean white field, with the green crown and dark brown beak as the only warm-ish accents. Black text and arrow give maximum contrast and the cool palette signals cold.
psychology: The bird shows round white eyeballs and an open beak, a stylised shock or distress cue, and the icicles supply a cold-danger cue. These are cartoon signals; no person appears.
partnership: The title says it sucks to be a hummingbird; the thumbnail gives the reason in three words with a visual of freezing. It leaves open how and why the bird dies each night, which sustains curiosity.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the wide-eyed bird head first, then the bold EVERY NIGHT, then the thin It Dies above it, with the arrow guiding back to the bird.
art: Heavily rendered semi-realistic illustration with ice-translucency effects. The chest is covered in fish-like scales rather than feathers and the wings are shaped from melted ice, which is stylised and not anatomically bird-like, but it reads as deliberate. The white background aids small-screen clarity.
strength: A single exaggerated image and a three-word claim explain the premise in under a second.
weakness: The thin It Dies line is visibly lighter than the heavy EVERY NIGHT capitals, so the two lines read as unequal in weight.
bottleneck: The scale-and-ice rendering is detailed and loses texture at 160x90, so only silhouette and colour carry the idea.
action: Hypothesis: set It Dies in the same heavy weight as EVERY NIGHT to test whether a uniform headline lifts the first-glance read.
counterexample: Seq 24 also uses a white ground but carries a diagram with tiny figures and no focal subject, where this frame has one huge subject.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: WE RUINED THIS?
scene: A smiling stick figure with closed curved eyes and an open grin reaches an arm toward a large pug on the right. The pug has a wrinkled snarling face with bared teeth, drool strands, red-veined bulging eyes and both front paws raised with claws out. The setting is a green backyard with a wooden fence, a tree, hedges and a few flowers.
mechanism: A cheerful stick figure meets a snarling dog, setting up the pet-domestication question as an obvious tonal clash between the friendly human and the hostile animal.
composition: The headline spans the top of the frame, the stick figure occupies the left third and the pug dominates the right half, creating a left-to-right confrontation. The pug is much bigger than the figure, giving it the primary focal weight, and the grassy foreground leaves clean space.
typography: Three words in thick yellow capitals with a black outline fill almost the full width at the top and stay fully readable at 160x90. The question mark invites an answer and the wording supplies the 'we' that the title phrases as 'do we'.
colors: Sky blue, mid-green lawn and tan pug give a bright, high-saturation daytime palette, and the yellow headline pops against the pale blue. The red veined eyes and white drool are the only small contrast accents.
psychology: The stick figure's closed-eye grin contrasts with the pug's bared teeth, flared brows and bulging eyes. That mismatch of expressions is the visible tension.
partnership: The title asks whether humans really spoil animals; the thumbnail answers with a monstrous pug and the word RUINED, which is stronger than the title's mild wording. It leaves open what exactly was ruined.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow headline first, then the snarling pug face, then the grinning stick figure's outstretched arm, with the garden last.
art: Flat cartoon with uniform outlines; the pug is rendered with more shading and detail than the plain stick figure, so two styles share one scene. Shadows under each figure fall consistently and the backyard stays simple.
strength: Opposing expressions on a stick figure and a pug turn a vague topic into an immediate visual joke.
weakness: The fence, tree and flower background add some busy detail behind the pug's head.
bottleneck: The word RUINED is not tied to any visible consequence besides the pug's face, so the claim stays open.
action: Hypothesis: add a visible before-state, such as a small wolf silhouette in a thought bubble beside the pug, to test whether showing what was ruined sharpens the story.
counterexample: Seq 6 uses the same yellow headline layout with three calm figures where this frame has a clear conflict pairing.
expression_label: grinning stick figure and snarling pug
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: BROKE [prop documents: PAST DUE with Amount Due $18,752.63; CREDIT CARD STATEMENT with BALANCE DUE $12,986.00; MORTGAGE PAYMENT OVERDUE; COLLECTION NOTICE FINAL NOTICE; LOAN PAYMENT DUE; Rolex watch box]
scene: A cartoon-faced man in a white suit and black shirt with a gold wristwatch sits on asphalt against a silver Porsche, one hand on his head and a PAST DUE bill in the other. Around him lie an open Rolex box with a watch, an empty brown wallet with a few coins, two Porsche key fobs, a golf bag at left, and several overdue and final-notice papers. A black arrow points from the headline down toward him.
mechanism: A rich-looking man surrounded by luxury objects and unpaid bills turns the title's 'looking rich' idea into a one-glance irony, with BROKE naming the outcome.
composition: The seated man sits slightly left of centre in a diagonal pose, with the car filling the top-left and bills spread across the bottom edge. The huge BROKE headline fills the top right and the arrow bridges it to the man, making a clear Z path, though the lower half is crowded with props.
typography: One word of thick red capitals with a white outline and a thin dark edge fills about a quarter of the frame and is the only text that survives at 160x90. The prop papers show digits and small print that blur away on mobile; BROKE repeats the title's last word without the 'looking rich' setup.
colors: Silver car and grey asphalt form a neutral ground; the white suit pops against it, and the red BROKE plus red OVERDUE and FINAL NOTICE stamps give a saturated red alarm accent. The green Rolex box adds a secondary colour spot.
psychology: Raised brows, wide round eyes and a hand pressed to the head show a stressed look, and red stamps on the papers add a financial-alarm cue. The wealth props set up the contrast.
partnership: The title delivers the brutal-truth framing and the #1 way; the thumbnail adds the proof that wealth props do not equal solvency through the Porsche, Rolex and bills. The title's explanatory twist is not shown, which keeps curiosity open.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: red BROKE first, then the man's face and white suit, then the PAST DUE paper he holds, then the Rolex box and bills along the bottom.
art: Realistic car, asphalt and prop textures are paired with a flat cartoon head on a more rendered body, and that style mismatch is visible at the neck and hairline. The overlapping scatter of papers and objects is dense, and the bill text is legible only at native size.
strength: Luxury objects plus overdue notices around one man tell the rich-but-broke story without needing the title.
weakness: Many small bills and props crowd the lower third and are unreadable on a phone.
bottleneck: Only BROKE survives at 160x90, so the evidence objects (Rolex, notices) reduce to colour blobs.
action: Hypothesis: crop to the man, the car badge and the PAST DUE sheet only, removing the golf bag and extra papers, to test whether fewer props improve small-size reading.
counterexample: Seq 5 shows a calm central figure in a crowd with a short headline, where this frame stacks many objects around the subject.
hero_object: BROKE headline with Porsche and overdue bills
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: FEEL BEHIND? [prop signs: elevator display 12; poster Retirement Info Session This Week]
scene: Inside a crowded elevator, a cartoon man in a navy cap and light-blue shirt stands in the centre with a plain round head, level brows and a flat mouth. Around him a woman in a green top laughs while holding a phone, a man in glasses smiles over two phones, and a bearded man holds a coffee cup. At least five more people are partly hidden behind and in the mirror at left. A red curved arrow points from the headline to the cap, and a poster beside the buttons reads Retirement Info Session This Week.
mechanism: One expressionless figure among laughing, phone-holding peers visualises the title's feeling of everyone being ahead, with a retirement poster hinting at the money topic.
composition: The capped man is the central, slightly oversized subject, flanked by three foreground figures in a shallow V. The yellow headline sits top-left and the red arrow runs from it to the cap, so the eye lands on the neutral face; the right edge is occupied by the elevator panel.
typography: Two words in thick yellow capitals with a black outline sit top-left on a busy mid-tone background, readable at 160x90 although it overlaps the warm background. The headline asks a feeling question and the retirement poster (too small to read on a phone) is the only money clue.
colors: Warm gold elevator walls and brown tones dominate, with saturated yellow text and a red arrow as the highlight accents. The man's light-blue shirt stands out against the warm background to separate him from the crowd.
psychology: The central figure has flat brows, a straight mouth and a forward stare while those around him have open smiles and broad eyes. The visible expression difference sets up an outsider contrast.
partnership: The title is a POV statement about others looking richer; the thumbnail turns it into a direct question and shows the contrast through the laughing crowd. The retirement poster is the only visible money link and it is tiny.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow FEEL BEHIND? first, then the red arrow to the capped man's blank face, then the laughing woman and the phone-holding man beside him.
art: Detailed cartoon illustration with soft shading and plausible elevator perspective, but the central man's head is a plain round shape with no nose while the neighbours are fully modelled, and that stylistic mismatch is deliberate-looking. The scene is crowded but the central figure remains legible at small size.
strength: The only still, blank-faced person in a laughing crowd makes the left-out feeling visible within a second.
weakness: The money cue (retirement poster) is too small to read on a phone, so the finance topic relies on the title.
bottleneck: The detailed crowd competes with the headline for attention and fills the whole background.
action: Hypothesis: reduce the crowd to two laughing figures and enlarge the retirement poster, to test whether a simpler scene makes the finance angle clearer.
counterexample: Seq 9 shows a lone success figure at a desk with no peer comparison, where this frame builds its meaning from a surrounding crowd.
expression_label: flat brows, neutral mouth among laughing people
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: SHARED WIVES?
scene: Three flat cartoon figures in brown hide tunics stand in a row on grass. At left a man with spiky brown hair has a flat mouth and eyes glancing right; in the middle a woman with long brown hair has wide eyes glancing left and a small open mouth; at right a man with spiky black hair smirks with eyes glancing left. Behind them are a thatched round hut, a green tree and two grey rocks under a cyan sky.
mechanism: Three side-glancing figures in an ancient village stage a triangle of looks, so the loaded question word pairs with an awkward-looking trio.
composition: The three figures are evenly spaced across the lower two thirds, with the woman at centre as a vertical divider and the hut and tree filling the gaps. The headline takes the whole top strip; the arrangement is symmetrical and static with no arrow or leading line.
typography: Two words in thick yellow capitals with a black outline span nearly the full frame width, large and easily readable at 160x90. The text drops the title's 'ancient humans' and 'why did', so the tunics and hut have to supply the era.
colors: Saturated cyan sky and bright green ground with brown tunics and a yellow headline make a loud primary-colour palette. Brown figures sit slightly low in contrast against the green but their white heads separate cleanly.
psychology: Side-glancing eyes on all three, a smirk on the right figure and a slightly parted mouth on the woman create a visible love-triangle tension. These are cartoon expressions only.
partnership: The title asks why ancient humans shared wives; the thumbnail compresses it to the two key words and shows the village setting. It adds no answer, leaving the why open.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow headline first, then the woman's wide eyes in the middle, then the smirking man at right, then the hut behind them.
art: Simple flat cartoon with thick outlines and no shading. The characters look near-identical stick-bodied templates with different hair, and the scene is easy to parse on a phone.
strength: A single loaded phrase in huge yellow text is legible at any size.
weakness: The figures are generic stick-style templates and the poses are static, so the picture adds little beyond the words.
bottleneck: No single object or action stands out, so the headline alone carries the hook.
action: Hypothesis: replace the static trio with a two-figure action, such as the two men facing each other with the woman between them gesturing, to test whether an interaction outperforms three standing looks.
counterexample: Seq 16 from the same channel uses a pointing gesture and a fire between figures, which adds action that this frame lacks.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: ACHILLES / IN 12 MINUTES
scene: A cartoon warrior with a gold crested helmet, a large red plume and a pale blank face with narrowed eyes and lowered brows raises a long grey spear tip toward the upper left. He holds a round bronze shield with a sunburst pattern at the right and wears a red cape. Behind him stand a wooden horse statue, a tan brick city wall, a sandy beach and a strip of sea under a blue sky with clouds.
mechanism: Instantly legible mythology iconography (crested helmet, spear, shield, wooden horse and walls) names the story and the 12-minute label sets a runtime promise.
composition: The warrior fills the centre with the spear diagonal slicing in from the upper left and the shield anchoring the lower right; the horse and wall add depth on the right. The text sits across the bottom third and overlaps the glove, shield rim and cape, which keeps the subject large but crowds the lower half.
typography: Four words in white outlined capitals on two lines, ACHILLES much larger than the IN 12 MINUTES line, sit across the lower middle. Both lines hold up at 160x90 against the saturated background, and the runtime numeral adds information the title does not give.
colors: Saturated blue sky, gold helmet and shield, a red cape and plume and tan sand make a warm-cool contrast. The white outlined text pops against the mid-tone cape and sand though it overlaps several colour regions.
psychology: Lowered brows and narrowed eyes under the helmet with a forward spear signal a combat stance. The expression is a flat cartoon cue and there is no direct gaze toward the viewer.
partnership: The title promises the entire story of the greatest Greek warrior; the thumbnail repeats the name and adds a short 12-minute runtime, which frames the long story as quick. It does not show any specific story event beyond the wooden horse.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the large ACHILLES wordmark first, then the crested helmet and face, then the spear tip at upper left, then the wooden horse behind the shoulder.
art: Bold-outlined cartoon with heavy black contour and cell shading, consistent lighting and coherent ancient-Greek props. The background is complex but sits behind a large foreground figure, and the helmet and plume read clearly at small size.
strength: Recognisable Greek-war iconography in strong colours makes the topic clear before any word is read.
weakness: The text overlaps the glove, shield and cape in the lower half and sits on a mid-tone region.
bottleneck: Visible information is a name and a runtime, so there is no question or conflict to resolve.
action: Hypothesis: add one specific story-hook element, such as a glowing mark on the heel, to test whether a hidden-weak-point cue lifts curiosity.
counterexample: Seq 8 puts one large headline question beside an unresolved question mark, which creates a curiosity gap this frame lacks.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: WHICH NUMBER / MATTERS? / LIPID PROFILE / LDL / HDL / ? / TRIGLYCERIDES
scene: A bearded man with dark swept-back hair and glasses, in navy scrubs with a stethoscope around his neck, holds both palms upward at the right. His eyebrows are slightly raised and his mouth is slightly open. At left is a white panel headed LIPID PROFILE with three rows labelled LDL (red bar), HDL (teal bar) and TRIGLYCERIDES (orange bar), blurred value digits and a large black question mark in a soft white glow. The background is dark and blurred with shelf shapes.
mechanism: An open-palm shrug beside a lab-result panel with hidden values turns the three cholesterol terms into an explicit which-one-matters question.
composition: The doctor-style figure occupies the right 40 percent, nearly facing the camera, and the chart panel the lower left, with the stacked headline above it. The question mark sits in the middle of the panel, forming a clear left-to-right path from headline to chart to the gesturing man.
typography: WHICH NUMBER in white and MATTERS? in large red capitals stack at the top left with high contrast on the dark ground. The chart's LDL and HDL labels remain readable at 160x90, while TRIGLYCERIDES is tiny and the blurred values are not legible. The thumbnail adds the which-matters question and leaves out the title's cardiologist wording.
colors: Near-black navy background with white and red headline, a navy scrub top and a white chart panel give strong separation. Red, teal and orange side bars on the chart colour-code the three lipids and add a small multi-colour accent.
psychology: Raised brows, a slightly open mouth, a direct gaze and upturned palms read as a questioning or explaining gesture with an authoritative scrubs-and-stethoscope setting. No fear imagery is shown.
partnership: The title lists LDL, HDL and triglycerides and names a cardiologist explanation; the thumbnail frames the same three terms as a which-one-matters question. It adds the hook and drops the credential, and the hidden numbers keep the answer unrevealed.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: red MATTERS first, then the man's face and gesturing hands, then the lipid panel with the question mark.
art: Photographic person on a dark studio background with a flat graphic panel composited at left. The panel's perspective is a simple flat card with a drop shadow, and the face lighting is consistent with the dark backdrop. Mobile survival is good for the headline and the man.
strength: Hidden digits behind a question mark create a clear unanswered question tied to the three named tests.
weakness: The credential only appears in the title and the TRIGLYCERIDES row is tiny on a phone.
bottleneck: The chart rows compete with the headline for text space, so the lipid labels shrink below easy reading size.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge the three row labels or reduce them to LDL and HDL only, to test whether a simpler chart improves the 160x90 read.
counterexample: Seq 14 uses a pointing arrow and a hand on the chest to push a fear framing, where this frame stays with a neutral question.
hero_object: lipid profile chart with question mark
medical_notes: Educational question framing about lab terms with no cure, diagnosis or fear claim, and the cardiologist credential appears only in the title.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: NONE
scene: A cartoon man in a navy suit and blue tie sits behind a wooden desk with a round white face, spiky dark hair, narrowed eyes and a one-sided smile, hands clasped. On the desk are a stack of green banknote bundles at left, a tablet showing a glowing gold rising arrow over blue bars in the middle, and a globe at right. Floor-to-ceiling windows behind him show a city skyline with two unfinished towers, a crane and a small jet.
mechanism: A wealth-empire tableau: cash, a growth chart, a globe and a skyline from a corner office suggest scale and ownership without any words.
composition: The man sits dead centre with the three desk props arranged symmetrically left to right, and the vertical window mullions frame him. The tablet arrow rises toward his hands, giving a small leading line, and the skyline sets the background depth.
typography: No text appears in the image, so the title carries all wording and nothing is lost or retained at 160x90 beyond shapes. The only readable-at-size elements are the stack of money and the gold arrow.
colors: Sky blue and steel-grey buildings dominate, with green banknotes at left and warm gold on the arrow and globe stand as the accent colours. The navy suit is darker than the sky but the white face pops against it.
psychology: A small smirk, narrowed eyes and a calm clasped-hands pose read as confident and at ease. There are no urgency or fear cues.
partnership: The title contrasts a business empire with a career; the thumbnail shows only the empire side as money, a rising chart and a skyline view. It offers no visible career counterpart, so the 'instead of' contrast is carried by the title alone.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the man's white face at centre first, then the cash stack at left, then the glowing gold arrow on the tablet, then the globe and skyline.
art: Smooth stylised illustration with consistent lighting, a flat white face on a more rendered suit, and plausible perspective on the desk and windows. The towers under construction and the plane are neat background detail that stays low-contrast at small size.
strength: Clear stacked symbols of wealth, growth and global scale make the empire idea readable without words.
weakness: No text and no career counterpart, so the instead-of tension from the title is absent.
bottleneck: The scene is a generic rich-office tableau that could front any wealth video.

colors: White ground with a muted dark-red and grey figure and a single red accent on the word No. The restrained palette separates the face cleanly and the red echoes the plaid shirt.

text: She had No Name [channel logo: Lost Legacy in a circular mark]
scene: A black-haired anime-style woman with narrow brown eyes, a closed mouth and a slight head tilt is shown from the chest up. text: PRIVACY?
scene: In a dark cave lit by a small campfire, a white-headed stick figure with lowered brows and a flat mouth hugs a long-haired figure whose eyes are closed and who has a small smile. Ten other figures in brown hide clothing, six on the left and four on the right, crowd the edges and all stare inward with frowns, narrowed eyes or side glances. Faint animal paintings appear on the cave wall at upper right.
mechanism: A hugging couple ringed by staring onlookers visualises the lack of privacy in a one-room prehistoric group, with a single question word as the headline.
composition: The embracing pair stands in the centre with the fire between the left crowd and the pair, and the watchers form a ring around the edges. The headline runs straight across the top and the ring structure compresses the centre, but the central pair stays the primary focus.
typography: One word with a question mark in thick yellow capitals with a black outline spans two thirds of the width and is readable at 160x90 against the dark cave. The word adds the specific topic that the title phrases as a private life.
colors: Dark brown and charcoal cave tones with a warm orange fire glow and a bright yellow headline. The white faces of the figures pop against the brown and the headline has the highest contrast of the frame.
psychology: The central figure's lowered brows and flat mouth, plus the ring of frowning and side-glancing faces, read as tension and scrutiny. The embraced figure's closed eyes and small smile contrast with the crowd.
partnership: The title asks how ancient humans had a private life; the thumbnail reduces it to PRIVACY? and shows the lack of it as a crowd looking at an embrace. It leaves open the answer to how they managed it.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow PRIVACY? first, then the central embracing pair, then the staring faces at the left and right edges, then the fire.
art: Flat cartoon on a darker textured cave background with a warm fire glow; the figures are repeated templates with different hair and angles. The overlapping crowd at the edges is dense, but the headline and the central pair hold up at small size.
strength: A ring of staring faces around an embrace turns a one-word headline into a clear visual joke.
weakness: Ten similar watcher faces repeat at the edges and add clutter without new information.
bottleneck: The repeated faces crowd the frame edges, and the dark cave lowers contrast for the smaller figures.
action: Hypothesis: reduce the watchers from ten to four larger ones, to test whether fewer, bigger staring faces improve the 160x90 read.
counterexample: Seq 6 uses three evenly spaced figures with no crowd, where this frame builds its meaning from a ring of onlookers.
expression_label: lowered brows, flat mouth, crowd of frowns

text: NONE [badge: what if?]
scene: A black-line drawing on white shows the corner of a house with a porch and shuttered window at the left. A pipe runs from its base to a small box and a larger box marked with a radiation trefoil, topped by a hopper of vibrating bananas. A featureless round-headed stick figure stands on a stepladder at the right, holding out a bunch of bananas. A red circle in the bottom-left corner holds a small black hanging-dinosaur drawing above the white words what if?.
mechanism: A deadpan line drawing connects a house to a banana-fuelled radiation box by a pipe, so the title's absurd power-plant idea is shown literally.
composition: The large house fills the left half with the machine and ladder figure small at the lower right, leaving the upper right empty. The pipe forms a long horizontal leading line between the two, and the red badge in the corner is the only colour.
typography: No headline text appears; the only words are the two small white words in the red badge, readable at 160x90 as a brand tag but not as a hook. The title carries all topic wording, including bananas, which the image shows only as tiny drawn objects.
colors: Black line art on white, with a single red circle in the corner as the colour accent. The red badge draws the eye despite its small size and the monochrome style is consistent.
psychology: The stick figure has a blank round head with no facial features, so no expression is visible. The stance holding out a banana bunch above a hopper is an offering gesture.
partnership: The title asks whether bananas could power a house; the thumbnail illustrates that exact setup with bananas, a radiation symbol and a house. It adds no text hook, so the intrigue depends on recognising the small objects.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the red what if? badge first, then the radiation symbol on the box, then the stick figure on the ladder, then the house at left.
art: Clean, consistent hand-drawn line style with uniform stroke weight and a large cropped house on the left. The bananas, vibration marks and stick figure are small and thin, so they lose detail at 160x90.
strength: The pipe from the house to the radiation box makes the banana-power idea literal and easy to follow at native size.
weakness: The key objects (bananas, figure) are tiny and the large house takes up half the frame.
bottleneck: The only readable words are the badge's what if?, which carries no information about bananas or houses.
action: Hypothesis: scale the banana hopper and radiation box to occupy the right half and shrink the house, to test whether a bigger machine improves the small-size read.
counterexample: Seq 2 puts one huge subject beside a bold phrase, where this frame uses tiny objects and no phrase.
